The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: ErrorRateSustained on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above 2.5% {A1} averaged over 10m {A2}
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T03:16:06Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T03:16:31Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 3 minutes 36 seconds {beyond_accounted_for} later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
Broken from 2026-11-11T03:10:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-11T03:30:55Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 20 minutes 55 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 14 minutes 27 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-11T03:30:55Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 19.1% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 37.0% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 18.3% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above 2.5% {A1} averaged over 10m {A2}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.875% {series_before} before it began, 19.142857142857142% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 37% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 8,253.46 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-11T03:10:18Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - [P2] 2026-11-11T03:17:04Z {P2.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by Argus: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched off
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 38 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 48 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 02:40–03:27 {G7e5d.4}. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:18,03:20–03:21,03:23–03:27 {G7e5d.5}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 46 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 48 {G46bc.2} minutes, 02:40–03:27 {G46bc.3}. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:18,03:20–03:21,03:23–03:27 {G46bc.4}

After Argus first acted, logged in 03:18–03:28 {Gbac1.8}

  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 22 {G5309.1} occurrences in 19 {G5309.2} minutes, 03:10–03:28 {G5309.3}. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:19,03:22,03:28 {G5309.4}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 9 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 18 {Gce95.3} minutes, 03:11–03:28 {Gce95.4}. After Argus first acted, logged in 03:19,03:22,03:28 {Gce95.5}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of monthly-spend-feature, each in its own words:
      C1: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-11T03:10:18Z {C1.1}. This enabled a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to about 32% {C1.3}. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, refuted]
      C2: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at 2026-11-11T03:10:18Z {C1.5}. Account page requests that evaluate it as on then fail with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Nothing was deployed and the rollout has converged. Errors follow the flag: they are high in minutes where evaluations show on and fall back to baseline in minutes where they show off. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.9 {C1.6}, refuted, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` computes `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)`. `bought_this_month` is the account's purchases filtered to `in_current_month`. Any shopper who has bought before but not this month gets an empty list, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. The page runs this code only when `use_monthly_summary` is true and `use_typical_spend` is false, which is why the errors followed monthly-spend-feature. The flag didn't create the fault. It sent ordinary idle shoppers into a divisor that is empty for them.
      
      The change: when nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0 {F1.1}. That means "no spend this month", not an error. Shoppers with purchases this month are handled exactly as before. The lifetime figure (`average_spend_per_item`), `render_spend_summary` and the request boundary are unchanged. A shopper with no purchase history at all still raises ZeroDivisionError from the lifetime figure when the flag is off, and the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py and tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py check for that failure. So nothing is being silenced: only the monthly figure's empty case now gets a defined answer.
      
      The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gets two new tests. One calls the monthly average directly for a shopper with purchases but none this month. The other renders through `render_spend_summary` with `use_monthly_summary=True`, the flag-on path. Both assert 0 {F1.2} is returned. Against the current code, both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #543 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out the shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing this month's total by the number of purchases made this month, in `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Nothing guards against an empty month, so a shopper who has bought before but not this month raises ZeroDivisionError and their account page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on account pages sent shoppers into a calculation that likely divides by the number of things they bought this month, and that fails for anyone who has not bought anything yet this month.
still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on, account pages could keep failing for any shopper who has bought before but not this month.
symptom: Account pages failed for shoppers
stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. To confirm it took effect, check at the service that account page requests log only monthly-spend-feature=off evaluations, with no monthly-spend-feature=on lines from any replica, and that ZeroDivisionError lines from src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop appearing.
why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether switching monthly-spend-feature off reached every replica and every flag evaluation. After the switch-off the service still logged the flag evaluating on in {Gce95.5}, and ZeroDivisionError in the same minutes ({G5309.4}). Find what kept serving the flag as on, and whether the error level the Mitigation Agent saw came from those minutes or from other errors.
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's error rate across all its requests rose far above its usual level. (cites AL1; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: Account page requests failed with ZeroDivisionError raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error was logged from the minute of onset onward, while before it account pages were logged rendering normally. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The requests reaching that code were the ones that evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on. Admin switched the flag on at {P1.1}, and from that minute the service logged it evaluating on for account page requests, alongside the errors. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: A deploy or other code change setting it off: the change events read back only the flag changes, all replicas ran the same revision, and account pages were logged rendering normally up to the minute before the flag was switched on. (cites T9, under "What Argus did, in order"; T30, under "What Argus did, in order"; T10, under "What Argus did, in order"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: Another flag change: apart from this one, the flag provider's history showed no flag change by anyone but Argus. (cites T15, under "What Argus did, in order"; T35, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 4: With the flag on, the account page divides this month's spend by the number of the shopper's purchases this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: No test or check was seen that ran the monthly-spend-feature path for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The empty-month division would have been found before any shopper reached it.
contributing_factors 2: The flag was not seen being rolled out in stages, and no automatic halt on rising errors was seen. In the minute it was switched on, most logged account page evaluations already read it as on.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: A small share of shoppers would have hit the fault, and the rollout could have stopped before it reached most account page traffic.
contributing_factors 3: The ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was paged.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: A person could have stepped in when switching the flag off did not end the errors, and kept the flag off rather than leaving it switched back on.
contributing_factors 4: The alert fired {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval, scraping allowance and onset minute account for. The record does not show what took the rest.
contributing_factors 4 had_it_been_otherwise: Argus would have started work on the incident sooner.
action_items 1: Before a feature flag on io-shop is switched on in production, require tests that run its flag-on path, including for shoppers with no purchases in the current period.
action_items 2: Roll out io-shop feature flags such as monthly-spend-feature in stages, by percentage of traffic, instead of switching them on for all traffic at once.
action_items 3: Halt a flag rollout on io-shop automatically, and turn the flag back off, when the account page error rate climbs after the flag change.
action_items 4: Link the ErrorRateSustained alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
action_items 5: Find out what delayed the ErrorRateSustained alert beyond what its evaluation interval, scraping allowance and onset minute account for, and remove that delay.
went_wrong 1: The Mitigation Agent judged the switch-off refuted and switched monthly-spend-feature back on. Yet after the switch-off, ZeroDivisionError was logged only in the minutes when the flag was still logged evaluating on ({G5309.4} and {Gce95.5}). Switching it back on likely let more account page requests evaluate it as on and reach the failing path. No log from after it was put back on was read.
went_wrong 2: Argus counted C2 as already tested by the switch-off and moved to FIXING with nothing further to try. But C2 said the errors followed the flag's evaluations minute by minute, which pointed to the switch-off not having taken hold everywhere rather than to the flag being innocent.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
